description:
# Flash Attention 2 — Forward Kernel

## Computes
Tiled scaled dot-product attention without materialising the full attention matrix. For each query row i:
  S_ij = Q_i · K_j^T * scale
  P_i  = softmax_j(S_ij)
  O_i  = sum_j P_ij * V_j
  lse_i = log(sum_j exp(S_ij))   (saved for the backward pass)

Optional features handled by the same kernel via compile-time switches: causal mask, local (sliding-window) mask, ALiBi additive bias, attention dropout, RoPE applied to Q/K, KV-cache append, multi-query / grouped-query attention, packed varlen (cu_seqlens), paged KV cache, soft-cap.

## I/O layout
- Q: `[B, H_q, Sq, D]`, K/V: `[B, H_kv, Sk, D]`, O: `[B, H_q, Sq, D]`, all fp16 or bf16, row-major contiguous.
- lse: `[B, H_q, Sq]` fp32.
- Strides are passed in `Flash_fwd_params`; varlen mode replaces B with cu_seqlens index.
- scale = 1 / sqrt(D) is precomputed by the host.

## Algorithm
Each thread block owns one Q row tile of `kBlockM` rows for one (batch, head_q). It iterates over K/V column tiles of `kBlockN` columns, maintaining per-row running statistics (m, l) and an accumulator acc_O in registers:

    for each K/V tile j:
      load K_tile, V_tile (cp.async)
      S = Q_tile @ K_tile^T * scale_log2     (in fp32 registers)
      apply mask (causal/local/alibi) if any
      m_new = max(m_old, rowmax(S))
      P = exp2(S - m_new)
      l_new = exp2(m_old - m_new) * l_old + rowsum(P)
      acc_O = exp2(m_old - m_new) * acc_O + P @ V_tile
      m_old, l_old = m_new, l_new
    O = acc_O / l_new
    lse = m_new * log(2) + log(l_new)

Working in log2 domain lets `exp2` use the dedicated EX2 hardware, halving the cost of the exponential.

## Tile structure
- Grid: `(num_m_blocks, B*H_q)` (or split-batch when num_splits > 1).
- Block: 128 or 256 threads = 4 or 8 warps.
- `Flash_fwd_kernel_traits<kHeadDim, kBlockM, kBlockN, kNWarps, ...>` selects MMA shape (m16n8k16 on Ampere), shared-memory swizzle, and Q/K/V smem layouts.
- kBlockM ≈ 128, kBlockN ≈ 32-128 depending on (kHeadDim, dtype, num_warps); larger kHeadDim shrinks kBlockN to fit smem.

## Key optimizations
- Online softmax: single pass over K, no second normalisation pass.
- log2 / exp2 + EX2 instruction instead of natural exp.
- cp.async double-buffered K and V loads overlapped with current-tile MMA.
- Shared-memory swizzling on Q/K/V/O matching mma.m16n8k16 fragment layout to avoid bank conflicts.
- Compile-time `Is_even_MN` / `Is_even_K` switches eliminate predicated copies on aligned shapes.
- Causal mask skips column tiles strictly below the diagonal — the kernel only enters the masked path on the diagonal tile.
- Optional GQA / MQA: H_q / H_kv ratio handled by index remap on K/V load.
- Optional split-batch (num_splits > 1) dispatched via `compute_attn_splitkv` (a separate module).

# Flash Attention 2 — Backward Kernel

## Computes
Given the upstream gradient dO and the saved forward tensors (Q, K, V, O, lse, scale), compute:
  dQ = dS @ K * scale
  dK = dS^T @ Q * scale
  dV = P^T @ dO
where dS = P · (dP - dsoftmax_sum), dP = dO @ V^T, P = exp(S - lse).

The full attention probabilities P are NOT materialized: they are recomputed tile-by-tile from saved Q, K, lse using the same softmax recurrence math as the forward pass.

## I/O layout
- dO, Q, K, V, O: `[B, H, S, D]` fp16/bf16. dQ, dK, dV: same layout.
- lse: `[B, H, Sq]` fp32 — saved by forward.
- dq_accum: `[B, H, seqlen_q_rounded, D]` fp32 (host-allocated scratch). dQ requires fp32 accumulation across K-tile iterations because multiple K-block CTAs write the same dQ row.
- dsoftmax_sum: `[B, H, seqlen_q_rounded]` fp32, prepared by the bwd_preprocess kernel = sum_d(dO * O).

## Algorithm
The backward parallelizes over **K-column tiles** (the opposite of forward). Each block owns one K/V column tile of `kBlockN` and iterates Q row tiles:

    load K_tile, V_tile into smem (held throughout)
    initialise dK_acc, dV_acc in registers
    for each Q row tile i:
      load Q_tile, dO_tile, lse_tile, dsoftmax_sum_tile
      S = Q_tile @ K_tile^T * scale
      apply mask (causal / local)
      P = exp(S - lse_tile)
      dV_acc += P^T @ dO_tile
      dP = dO_tile @ V_tile^T
      dS = P * (dP - dsoftmax_sum_tile)
      dQ_partial = dS @ K_tile * scale       (fp32)
      atomicAdd onto dq_accum[i_row, :]
      dK_acc += dS^T @ Q_tile * scale
    write dK_acc, dV_acc as dK[:, n_block, :], dV[:, n_block, :]

A separate post-process kernel converts dq_accum (fp32) to dQ in fp16/bf16.

## Tile structure
- Grid: `(num_n_blocks, B * H)` — one CTA per K/V tile.
- Two layouts available: parallel-over-K (default) and parallel-over-K-with-seqq-parallel (`compute_dq_dk_dv_seqk_parallel`) trading dq_accum atomics for an extra reduction.
- Block: 128 or 256 threads (8 warps for hdim ≤ 128, 4 warps for hdim ≥ 192).
- `Flash_bwd_kernel_traits` picks (kBlockM, kBlockN, num_warps, smem layout) per (kHeadDim, dtype, causal).

## Key optimizations
- One kernel computes dQ, dK, dV; only one re-load of Q per tile pair.
- dQ uses fp32 accumulator (dq_accum) + atomicAdd because multiple K blocks contribute to the same Q row; dK and dV stay in registers and are written exactly once.
- `dsoftmax_sum` precomputed by preprocess kernel removes the `sum_d(dO * O)` cost from the inner loop.
- Causal mask: when in the strictly-upper-triangle region (j < i_min) the inner loop is skipped entirely.
- All MMAs use Ampere mma.m16n8k16 with shared-memory swizzling consistent with the forward kernel.
- `is_seqlen_k_cumulative` and `unpadded_lse` switches handle varlen mode without runtime branches in the hot loop.

# Flash Attention 2 — Online Softmax Recurrence

## Computes
Streaming numerically-stable softmax that produces P_i = exp(S_i - max_i) / sum(exp(S_i - max_i)) across multiple K column tiles **without revisiting tiles**, suitable for the FA2 forward and backward inner loops.

Maintained per query row i:
  m_i — running maximum of S so far
  l_i — running sum of exp(S - m_i)
  acc_O_i — running unnormalised output accumulator (forward only)

When a new tile's scores S_tile arrive:
  m_new = max(m_i, rowmax(S_tile))
  rescale = exp2(m_i - m_new)
  l_new = rescale * l_i + rowsum(exp2(S_tile - m_new))
  acc_O = rescale * acc_O + exp2(S_tile - m_new) @ V_tile        (forward)

After the last tile: O = acc_O / l_new, lse = m_new * log(2) + log(l_new).

## I/O layout
The Softmax struct lives entirely in registers; no global I/O of its own. It exposes per-row state arrays of length `kNRows = kBlockM / num_warps_per_row`. Scores S enter as a CuTe `Tensor` over MMA fragments laid out for `mma.m16n8k16`.

## Algorithm
Implemented as a templated `Softmax<kNRows>` struct in softmax.h with three primary methods:
  - `template_rescale_o_lse_sum` (or `softmax_rescale_o`): reduces rowmax across the warp via butterfly shuffle, computes rescale factor, applies it to acc_O and l, adds rowsum of new exp tile.
  - `template_to_p` / similar: converts the post-shift S into P = exp2(S - m_new) for the P @ V matmul.
  - `template_finalize`: final divide-by-l and log to produce O and lse.

The reduction pattern is a *partial* warp reduce — only across the `num_threads_per_row` lanes that hold a row, not the full 32 — so it composes with the MMA register layout.

## Tile structure
- Per-row state stored as fp32 in registers: `m[kNRows]`, `l[kNRows]`.
- Score tile S has shape `(kNRowsPerThread, kNColsPerThread)` per thread, derived from `mma.m16n8k16` fragments.
- `kNRows` = MMA M-tile rows assigned to this warp = `kBlockM / num_warps_per_M`.

## Key optimizations
- Works in log2 domain so the exponential becomes a hardware `exp2` (EX2 SFU instruction) — ~3× cheaper than `__expf`.
- Rowmax / rowsum reductions reuse the existing warp-level shuffle pattern from CUTLASS so the compiler can fold them with the surrounding MMA.
- Avoids the write-back-and-read-again pattern of naive 3-pass softmax: O accumulator is rescaled in place when m changes.
- Templated on `Is_first` (first K tile takes the fast path with no rescale) and `Check_inf` (skips rescale when m is already -inf, e.g. after a fully-masked tile in causal mode).
- The same Softmax struct is reused by the backward to recompute P from saved lse without rescaling.

# Flash Attention 2 — Score Masking

## Computes
Applies position-dependent additive bias / score zeroing to the pre-softmax score tile S = Q @ K^T * scale before the online softmax sees it. Three orthogonal modes selectable at compile time:

- **Causal**:        S[i, j] = -inf for j > i (relative to the global token index, accounting for sequence-length difference between K and Q).
- **Local** (sliding window): S[i, j] = -inf for j < i - window_left  OR  j > i + window_right.
- **ALiBi**:         S[i, j] += slope[h] * (j - i)   (negative for j < i; combines with causal/local).

All three may stack: causal-with-ALiBi is the standard Llama-style configuration.

## I/O layout
The score tile S is held in registers in MMA fragment layout `(kNRowsPerThread, kNColsPerThread)` per thread. The mask is computed from the tile's logical (m_block_row_start, n_block_col_start) origin plus the per-thread fragment offset; no global memory traffic.

## Algorithm
A templated struct `Mask<Is_causal, Is_local, Has_alibi>`:

    apply_mask(S, col_idx_offset, row_idx_offset, warp_row_stride):
      for each (frag_i, frag_j) in S:
        global_row = row_idx_offset + frag_i offset
        global_col = col_idx_offset + frag_j offset
        if Is_causal and global_col > global_row + (Sk - Sq):
            S[frag_i, frag_j] = -INFINITY
        elif Is_local:
            if global_col < global_row + (Sk - Sq) - window_left or
               global_col > global_row + (Sk - Sq) + window_right:
                S[frag_i, frag_j] = -INFINITY
        if Has_alibi:
            S[frag_i, frag_j] += slope * (global_col - global_row)

The kernel is structured to skip mask application entirely when the entire tile is on the safe side of the diagonal (for causal) or window boundary, by issuing a `max_seqlen_q_minus` / `max_seqlen_k_minus` compile-time-style check in the outer K-tile loop.

## Tile structure
- Operates on the same MMA fragments held in registers — no smem use.
- The "diagonal tile" path (where causal mask intersects the tile) is the only one that pays masking overhead; fully-below-diagonal tiles are skipped and fully-above-diagonal tiles are pre-zeroed.
- ALiBi slope per head is loaded once per CTA from `params.alibi_slopes_ptr`.

## Key optimizations
- Compile-time predication (`Is_causal`, `Is_local`, `Has_alibi`) eliminates dead branches.
- The (Sk - Sq) shift is precomputed once per kernel; relative position math becomes a single integer add per fragment.
- Masking is fused into the same loop that converts S to P (no separate pass over the score tile).
- The diagonal-tile optimization caps causal masking cost at one tile per Q row.
- ALiBi slope multiplication uses fp32 fmadd, fused with the subsequent `exp2` argument formation.

# Flash Attention 2 — Rotary Position Embedding (RoPE)

## Computes
Applies rotary position embedding to Q and K **on the fly**, before the QK^T matmul, so that the attention kernel sees position-encoded queries / keys without an extra global-memory round trip.

For each pair (x_2k, x_2k+1) at position p with rotary frequency θ_k:

    x'_2k     =  x_2k * cos(p θ_k) - x_2k+1 * sin(p θ_k)
    x'_2k+1   =  x_2k * sin(p θ_k) + x_2k+1 * cos(p θ_k)

Two layouts supported:
- **Interleaved** (GPT-NeoX / Llama): the pair is `(x_2k, x_2k+1)`.
- **Non-interleaved** (HuggingFace): the pair is `(x_k, x_{k + D/2})` — i.e. first half rotated against second half.

Only the first `rotary_dim` channels are rotated; the remaining `D - rotary_dim` channels pass through unchanged.

## I/O layout
- Cos / sin table: `[Sq, rotary_dim/2]` fp16/bf16, indexed by absolute position `p`.
- For decode + KV cache the K positions are offset by `cache_seqlens` (the past length per batch element).
- Operates on Q / K already loaded into shared memory; result is written back to the same smem tile.

## Algorithm
Two templated copy-and-rotate device functions: one for the interleaved variant, one for the non-interleaved variant. Both run as a separate predicated copy pass before the K/V load:

    for each (warp, lane) covering the Q (or K) tile:
      load 4 elements (2 real pairs) from gmem, with cp.async if available
      look up cos[p, k], sin[p, k]
      apply 2x2 rotation in fp32 (cast back to fp16 on store)
      store into smem in the same swizzled layout the MMA expects

Compile-time switches:
- `Is_even_K` skips the masked-tail predication on `rotary_dim`.
- `Clear_OOB_K` zeroes channels beyond `rotary_dim` if the smem tile is wider.

## Tile structure
- Reuses the kBlockM × kHeadDim Q smem tile and kBlockN × kHeadDim K smem tile.
- One thread covers `kElemsPerLoad` real elements (typically 8 fp16).
- The cos/sin table is small enough (Sq × rotary_dim/2) to be cached in L1.

## Key optimizations
- Fused with the Q/K smem load — no separate kernel launch and no extra gmem write.
- fp32 rotation arithmetic, fp16 / bf16 storage — preserves precision near the cos/sin boundary at zero.
- Cos / sin shared across all heads of a block, loaded once per K tile.
- Predicated `cp.async` for tail tokens when Sq is not divisible by kBlockM.
- Decode path uses `cache_seqlens` to compute per-batch position offsets without rebuilding the cos/sin table.

# Flash Attention 3 — Forward Kernel (SM80 path)

## Computes
The Ampere / Ada (sm80, sm86, sm89) forward attention kernel from FlashAttention v3. Same scaled dot-product attention as FA2 forward, but rebuilt on top of CUTLASS / CuTe primitives so the same kernel template can be specialised for sm80 (this module) and sm90 (separate module). Outputs O and lse, supports causal / local / softcap / GQA / KV cache / paged KV / packed varlen.

Differences from FA2 forward (sm80):
- All loads / MMAs expressed via CuTe `Tensor` and `gemm()` calls instead of hand-written cp.async + ldmatrix sequences.
- Block / warp layout is parameterised by `TileShape_MNK` and `ClusterShape_MNK` rather than hard-coded constants.
- The "mainloop" is factored into a separate header (`mainloop_fwd_sm80.hpp`) so the same K-tile recurrence can be reused by sm90 (different mainloop) and the combine kernel.
- Provides hooks for paged KV (block-table based) and pack_gqa indexing.

## I/O layout
Same as FA2 forward: Q/K/V/O `[B, H, S, D]`, lse `[B, H, Sq]`. Strides come through `Flash_fwd_params` defined in `flash.h`. The seqlen handling lives in `seqlen.h` and supports four modes: dense, varlen (cu_seqlens), KV-cache append (cache_seqlens), paged (block_table).

## Algorithm
Mostly identical to FA2 forward (Q-row tile parallelism, online softmax recurrence over K column tiles), with the pieces wired through CuTe:

    SM80 mainloop (CollectiveMainloopFwdSm80):
      construct gQ, gK, gV global tensors; partition them by tile shape
      pre-issue cp.async on first K, V tile
      while n_block > n_block_min:
        gemm(QxK^T → S in fp32)     // CuTe gemm wraps mma.m16n8k16
        apply_mask(S)
        softmax.online_step(S, acc_O)
        copy_async(next K, V)
        gemm(P x V → acc_O)
      epilogue: rescale by 1/l, write O via cp.async-bulk where available, write lse

    Kernel (FlashAttnFwdSm80) launches with:
      grid = scheduler.get_grid()
      block = num_warps * 32
      shared memory holds Q (one tile), K (double buffered), V (double buffered)

## Tile structure
- TileShape_MNK = (kBlockM, kBlockN, kHeadDim) selected by `tile_size.h::tile_size_fwd_sm80(kHeadDim, dtype)`.
- Single cluster (no inter-CTA TMA on sm80).
- Smem capacity check at compile time via `static_assert(smem_size <= 100 KB)` because sm80 caps shared memory at ~100 KB.
- No persistent scheduling — one CTA per (m_block, B*H) just like FA2.

## Key optimizations
- cp.async multi-stage pipeline: 2 stages on K, 2 on V — overlaps with the QK^T and PV matmuls.
- Reuses the FA2 swizzling on Q/K/V smem layouts for bank-conflict-free MMA.
- Online softmax in log2 domain (calls into the v3 Softmax struct).
- Compile-time static_switch on (Is_causal, Is_local, Has_alibi, Has_softcap, Is_paged_KV, packed_GQA) — eliminates dead branches.
- Reuses CUTLASS predicated copies for tail tiles, no manual index math in the kernel body.
- Same kernel handles dense and paged KV via a small `TensorKVMaker` helper that returns the right global tensor.
- This sm80 path is what runs on Ampere/Ada (the sm90 path requires Hopper TMA + WGMMA, separate module).

# Flash Attention 3 — Forward Combine Kernel

## Computes
Reduces the per-split partial outputs produced by the split-KV forward kernel into the final attention output. Given:

  O_accum:   `[num_splits, B, H, Sq, D]` fp32
  lse_accum: `[num_splits, B, H, Sq]` fp32

produce:

  m_global = max_s lse_accum[s]
  weight_s = exp(lse_accum[s] - m_global)
  O_final = sum_s weight_s * O_accum[s] / sum_s weight_s
  lse_final = m_global + log(sum_s weight_s)

This is the second half of the split-KV pipeline; the first half (`fa3/fwd_sm80` or `fa3/fwd_sm90` with split scheduler) writes the per-split partials.

## I/O layout
- Inputs: O_accum and lse_accum as above. num_splits is small (typically 2 - 16).
- Outputs:
  - O: `[B, H, Sq, D]` fp16/bf16 — the final attention output.
  - lse: `[B, H, Sq]` fp32 — the final log-sum-exp (only needed when the user requested it; otherwise skipped via the `Output_lse` template flag).

## Algorithm

    blockIdx = (m_block, B * H)
    threads cooperate over kBlockM rows × D columns

    for each row i in tile:
      // step 1: find global max over splits
      m_global = -inf
      for s in 0..num_splits:
        m_global = max(m_global, lse_accum[s, b, h, i])

      // step 2: compute weights and normaliser
      sum_w = 0
      for s in 0..num_splits:
        w[s] = (lse_accum[s] == -inf) ? 0 : exp(lse_accum[s] - m_global)
        sum_w += w[s]

      // step 3: weighted reduction over D
      for d-vec covered by this thread:
        acc = 0
        for s in 0..num_splits:
          acc += w[s] * O_accum[s, b, h, i, d-vec]
        O[b, h, i, d-vec] = (T_out)(acc / sum_w)

      if Output_lse:
        lse[b, h, i] = m_global + log(sum_w)

## Tile structure
- Grid: `(num_m_blocks, B * H)`.
- Block: 128 threads in a `(num_threads_per_row, num_rows_per_block)` 2D layout — same as bwd_postprocess.
- num_splits is small enough that per-thread `w[]` fits in registers.
- No shared memory needed beyond the cooperative reduction along D within a warp.

## Key optimizations
- The reduction over splits is small and fully in-register; no smem traffic for w[s].
- Vectorised global loads of O_accum (uint4 = 4 fp32 / 8 fp16 per thread) along the D axis.
- Skips splits whose `lse_accum == -inf` (empty K range, e.g. fully-masked-by-causal split) without arithmetic.
- The `Output_lse` switch removes the lse write when the caller doesn't need it.
- Memory-bound by design — runs in microseconds for typical decode workloads (Sq=1, B*H≪SM count, num_splits=4-8).
- This kernel is what makes split-KV practical: without it the "more occupancy" benefit of splits would be wiped out by an extra global-memory normalization pass on the host.

# Flash Attention 3 — Backward Kernel (SM80 path)

## Computes
The Ampere / Ada (sm80) backward kernel from FlashAttention v3. Same dQ / dK / dV computation as FA2 backward, refactored on CUTLASS / CuTe so the K-tile parallel mainloop can be reused by sm90.

  dV = P^T @ dO
  dP = dO @ V^T
  dS = P · (dP - dsoftmax_sum)
  dQ = dS @ K * scale       (atomicAdd onto fp32 dq_accum)
  dK = dS^T @ Q * scale

P is recomputed from saved Q, K, lse — never materialised in memory.

## I/O layout
Same as FA2 backward via `Flash_bwd_params`: dO/Q/K/V/O fp16/bf16, lse fp32, dsoftmax_sum fp32, dq_accum fp32. Adds:
- Optional paged KV through `block_table_ptr`.
- Optional packed varlen with `cu_seqlens_q / cu_seqlens_k`.
- Soft-cap support via `params.softcap` (the tanh-based score clamp common in Gemma).

## Algorithm
Same K-tile-parallel structure as FA2 backward, but the inner loop is expressed as CuTe gemms and copies, with the mainloop factored into `mainloop_bwd_sm80.hpp`:

    SM80 backward mainloop:
      load K_tile, V_tile into smem (held throughout)
      initialise dK_acc, dV_acc in registers
      for q row tile in [m_block_min, m_block_max):
        copy_async(Q, dO, lse, dsoftmax_sum)
        gemm(QxK^T → S)
        apply_mask(S)
        if Has_softcap: S = softcap * tanh(S / softcap)
        P = exp(S - lse)
        gemm(P^T x dO → dV_acc)
        gemm(dO x V^T → dP)
        if Has_softcap: dP *= (1 - tanh(S/softcap)^2)
        dS = P * (dP - dsoftmax_sum)
        gemm(dS x K → dQ_partial)
        atomicAdd dQ_partial onto dq_accum[q_row, :]
        gemm(dS^T x Q → dK_acc)
      write dK_acc, dV_acc to dK[n_block], dV[n_block]

The kernel shell is in `flash_bwd_kernel_sm80.h`; epilogue handles the dK/dV write and final cast-to-output-dtype path.

## Tile structure
- Grid: `(num_n_blocks, B * H)`.
- TileShape_MNK selected by `tile_size.h::tile_size_bwd_sm80(kHeadDim, dtype, causal)`.
- Block: 128 or 256 threads — typically 8 warps for hdim ≤ 128, 4 warps for hdim ≥ 192 to keep smem within sm80 limits.
- K and V are held in smem for the entire q-tile loop; Q, dO, lse, dsoftmax_sum are double-buffered and streamed.

## Key optimizations
- K-tile-parallelism: dK and dV stay in registers, written exactly once. Only dQ pays the atomicAdd cost.
- cp.async multi-stage pipeline on Q / dO; K and V pinned in smem (loaded once per CTA).
- All MMAs through CuTe `gemm()` which lowers to mma.m16n8k16 + appropriate ldmatrix on sm80.
- Soft-cap derivative `dP *= 1 - tanh^2(S/softcap)` fused into the existing dS computation.
- Compile-time switches on `Is_causal`, `Is_local`, `Has_softcap`, `Is_packed_varlen`, `Is_paged_KV` — same static_switch pattern as forward.
- Falls back from sm90 path on non-Hopper hardware automatically.
- This is the path the benchmark uses on the L40 / RTX PRO 6000 / A100 / H100-no-WS configurations.

# Flash Attention 3 — Online Softmax Recurrence

## Computes
The FA3 version of the online softmax. Same numerical recurrence as the FA2 Softmax struct (running max, running sum_exp, in-place output rescale), but redesigned to operate on WGMMA register fragments and to compose with FA3's warp-specialized pipeline.

Maintained per query row i:
  m — running max
  l — running sum of exp(S - m)
  acc_O — running unnormalised output accumulator

On a new tile S_tile:
  m_new = max(m, rowmax(S_tile))
  rescale = exp2(m - m_new)
  acc_O = rescale * acc_O + (P = exp2(S_tile - m_new)) @ V_tile
  l = rescale * l + rowsum(P)

## I/O layout
The Softmax struct is templated on:
  `<int kNRows, int kNCols, bool Use_max_offset = false>`
where `kNRows` = MMA M-rows owned by this thread, `kNCols` = MMA N-cols. State `m`, `l` lives in fp32 register arrays of length `kNRows`. The score tile arrives as a CuTe register `Tensor` whose layout matches a WGMMA accumulator on sm90 (and m16n8k16 on sm80).

## Algorithm
Three primary methods:

    online_softmax_step(S_tile, V_load_handle):
      // 1. row-reduce max across the warp group
      rowmax = warpgroup_reduce_max(S_tile)
      m_new = max(m, rowmax)
      rescale = exp2(m - m_new)

      // 2. rescale prior accumulator and l in registers
      acc_O *= rescale          // broadcast across cols
      l *= rescale

      // 3. compute P = exp2(S_tile - m_new) — WGMMA-fragment-shaped
      P = exp2(S_tile - m_new)

      // 4. add new tile's row sum
      l += warpgroup_reduce_sum(P)

      // 5. accumulate P @ V_tile into acc_O (caller does this with a wgmma)
      m = m_new

    finalize(acc_O, l, m):
      O = acc_O * (1 / l)        // 1/l from rcp.approx for speed
      lse = m * log(2) + log(l)

The "max offset" variant (Use_max_offset = true) shifts S by a per-row constant before exp to keep the exponent argument in the WGMMA register's representable range when the score range exceeds ~85.

## Tile structure
- State entirely in registers: `m[kNRows]`, `l[kNRows]`, both fp32.
- Reduction across the warp group (128 threads) for sm90, or across a single warp on sm80.
- The reduction pattern is partial — only the lanes that hold a row participate, matching the WGMMA fragment layout.

## Key optimizations
- Operates in log2 domain → uses `ex2.approx.f32` (EX2 SFU instruction).
- Warp-group-level reduction on sm90 uses `warpgroup_reduce` from CUTLASS — single barrier-free shuffle pattern across 128 lanes.
- `Is_first` and `Check_inf` template flags eliminate the rescale on the first tile and skip rescale when m == -inf (fully-masked tile in causal mode).
- The "max offset" variant trades one fmadd for the ability to handle longer numerical range — useful for soft-capped or extremely-long-context attention where score variance is wider.
- Reused unchanged by the FA3 backward to recompute P from saved lse (the same exp2(S - lse) pattern), so writing this struct correctly buys both forward and backward.

# Flash Attention 3 — Score Masking

## Computes
The FA3 version of the score-mask module. Applies position-dependent masking and bias to the pre-softmax score tile S = Q @ K^T * scale before the online softmax. Supports the same modes as FA2 plus two FA3 additions:

- **Causal**:        S[i, j] = -inf for j > i (with K-Q sequence-length offset).
- **Local** (sliding window): S[i, j] = -inf outside [i - left, i + right].
- **Soft-cap** (Gemma-style): S[i, j] = softcap * tanh(S[i, j] / softcap), applied before any other mask.
- **ALiBi** is implemented via the bias argument to the score load on FA3, not in the Mask struct.

The struct is parameterised on `<bool Is_causal, bool Is_local, bool Has_softcap>` so unused branches are dead-code-eliminated.

## I/O layout
- Operates on the score tile S held in WGMMA accumulator registers (on sm90) or m16n8k16 fragments (on sm80) — same layout as the Softmax struct expects.
- Reads `params.window_size_left`, `window_size_right`, `softcap` once per CTA.
- For paged KV the column index is rebuilt from the block_table — masking still uses the *logical* column index, not the storage index.

## Algorithm

    template <bool Is_causal, bool Is_local, bool Has_softcap>
    struct Mask {
      apply_mask(S, m_block, n_block, q_seqlen, k_seqlen):
        for each (frag_i, frag_j) in S:
          q_global = m_block * kBlockM + frag_i offset
          k_global = n_block * kBlockN + frag_j offset
          // optional soft-cap first (acts on every element)
          if Has_softcap:
            S[frag_i, frag_j] = softcap * tanh(S[frag_i, frag_j] / softcap)
          // causal / local masking
          if Is_causal and k_global > q_global + (k_seqlen - q_seqlen):
            S[frag_i, frag_j] = -INFINITY
          elif Is_local and (k_global < q_global - window_left or
                             k_global > q_global + window_right):
            S[frag_i, frag_j] = -INFINITY
    }

The "diagonal tile" optimisation present in FA2 mask is preserved: the outer K-tile loop in the kernel skips fully-below-diagonal tiles (causal) and fully-out-of-window tiles (local), so the mask only fires on boundary tiles.

## Tile structure
- Pure register operation; no shared memory.
- Per-fragment offsets are precomputed once per warp-group iteration to avoid recomputing `(q_global, k_global)` per element.
- For sm90 the WGMMA fragment has shape (16, 16) per thread group; for sm80 it's m16n8k16.

## Key optimizations
- Compile-time predication on `Is_causal`, `Is_local`, `Has_softcap` — zero overhead when off.
- Soft-cap uses `__tanhf` plus a single fmul/fdiv pair; the derivative needed by backward is recomputed in `bwd_preprocess` from saved S, not stored.
- The diagonal-tile + outer-loop boundary optimisation caps mask cost at one tile per Q row regardless of sequence length.
- Reuses `seqlen.h` to compute the (k_seqlen - q_seqlen) shift once per kernel.
- Composes with the warp-specialized pipeline on sm90: the consumer warp groups apply the mask without needing to re-synchronise with the producer.

# Flash Attention 3 — Tile Scheduler

## Computes
The FA3 persistent-CTA work scheduler. Replaces a static `grid = (num_m_blocks, B*H, num_splits)` launch with a small set of persistent CTAs (one per SM) that loop over work items themselves. Three flavours selectable at compile time:

1. **StaticTileScheduler** — grid is fixed at launch as `(num_m_blocks, B*H, splits)` — the trivial scheduler, used by FA2 forward.
2. **DynamicPersistentTileScheduler** — `numSMs` CTAs are launched; each pulls work items from a global atomic counter. Better load balance for varlen / heterogeneous batches.
3. **VarlenDynamicPersistentTileScheduler** — same as above but the work-item indexing accounts for cu_seqlens, packed-varlen mode.

This module is the scheduler infrastructure; the actual mainloop runs once per work item the scheduler hands out.

## I/O layout
- The scheduler reads kernel params (B, H, Sq, num_splits, optional cu_seqlens / block_table) and exposes:
    `WorkTileInfo get_next_work(int cta_id)`
    `bool is_valid(WorkTileInfo info)`
    `int get_total_num_blocks()`     // host helper
- WorkTileInfo holds `(m_block, batch_idx, head_idx, split_idx)`.
- For dynamic schedulers a single global `int counter` is used as the atomic work queue.

## Algorithm

    StaticTileScheduler:
      blockIdx → (m_block, batch * head, split)   // direct mapping

    DynamicPersistentTileScheduler:
      cta_id = blockIdx.x
      lane 0 of warp 0 atomically increments global counter to claim a work item
      broadcast that index to the whole CTA via smem
      decode (m_block, batch, head, split) from the linear index
      kernel runs the mainloop on this work item
      goto top until counter ≥ total_num_blocks

    VarlenDynamicPersistentTileScheduler:
      same as Dynamic, but the linear index decode walks cu_seqlens to find which batch
      the m_block belongs to (binary search done once at the start of each work item)

For sm90 the dynamic schedulers also issue `mbarrier.try_wait` on a "scheduler ready" signal so consumer warp groups can pre-fetch the K/V TMA descriptors of the next work item while the current one is finishing.

## Tile structure
- Persistent grid: launches exactly `num_SMs * cta_per_sm` CTAs (queried via `cudaOccupancyMaxActiveBlocksPerMultiprocessor` at host side).
- One smem slot per CTA holds the broadcast work-item index (8 bytes).
- For Hopper (sm90) the scheduler uses cluster-aware launch when ClusterShape > (1,1,1); each cluster shares one work item.

## Key optimizations
- Persistent CTAs eliminate the launch overhead of having a large grid for short-Sq decode workloads (where launch latency dominates).
- Dynamic atomic-counter scheduling balances load across SMs when batches have very different sequence lengths (varlen) — typical for inference batching.
- Binary search over cu_seqlens is done once per work item, not per token, so its cost amortises across kBlockM rows.
- The scheduler is the FA3 piece that makes very-long-context (Sq up to 1M) inference practical: with static grids the load imbalance from masked tiles in causal mode wastes ~50% of SM time; dynamic scheduling cuts that to <5%.
- Compile-time choice between the three schedulers means non-varlen training paths pay zero overhead for the persistent infrastructure.
